paragraphs: Chapter 1132
Episode 259. The Truth of the World, Your Truth, My Truth (1)
[Go, kid!]
Murakan shouted, spewing black blood. While he was boring a hole in the sea with his breath, the awls of light had pierced him dozens of times.
Are you okay? He didn't even have the leisure to look back at Murakan, let alone ask such a thing.
With Kelliac having almost regained his senses, a more elaborate and cruel attack was sure to begin.
How many deaths were there to find this unknown black barrier? Jin had already gritted his teeth and thrown his body.
"I'm counting on you!"
"Where do you...!"
Just before Jin reached the sanctuary, Kelliac's eyes snapped open and he pinpointed his exact location.
He aimed and dropped the light, and filled the crack in the sea.
He also transformed the seawater spread around Jin into sharp solids.
Light and red blades pierced and cut Jin's body all over as he descended.
There were also blades that had lodged deep enough to catch on bone and organs.
But in the end, Jin, still breathing, disappeared into the black barrier.
"Hah."
A low sigh escaped Kelliac. Murakan, on the other hand, grinned even as his wings were being torn to shreds.

[What are you gonna do now, Kelliac Zipple? You should have focused a little more on us instead of the kid. Then I wouldn't have been able to escape your disgusting desire and help the kid like this.]
Kelliac didn't answer and kept his gaze on the red sea where Jin had disappeared.
As Murakan said, Kelliac had been so concerned with Jin that he hadn't noticed the weakening of the red sea's power.
His obsession with Jin had ruined things.
If he had truly trampled his enemies with the composure of a one true god, such an absurd situation would never have happened in the first place.
Suddenly, Kelliac appeared right in front of Murakan, in the spot where Jin had disappeared.
Teleportation. Kelliac paid no mind to Murakan, who was hastily trying to create distance, and looked down at the sea.
With a light wave of his hand, the sea parted to both sides, revealing the black barrier again.
Solderet's final legacy. Kelliac roughly dropped a pillar of light onto it.
But the barrier only shimmered like water, showing no signs of being destroyed at all.
Even when he descended and tried to enter the barrier directly, there was no reaction.
Moreover, a moment later, the barrier blurred and showed signs of disappearing as if seeping into space.
Even when he strained his senses, nothing was caught. He could no longer track Jin.
That is your limit. Kelliac chewed on the words Jin had just said and extended a hand over the water's surface.
Then, a pure white staff shot up from beneath the sea and coiled around his hand.
It was the Origin Stone, its restoration just completed.
"...Yes, it seems today is a day I've been made a fool of several times. But from now on, you all will not be able to remember the fact that a person named Jin Runcandel ever existed in this world."
"Keuh-euk..."
Spitting out a mouthful of blood, Jin recalled the recent memory.
It was the moment he had cut the barrier by swinging Barisada.
At that very moment, he had been pierced by Kelliac's light and the sharply solidified red seawater, and had almost lost consciousness.
A hole the size of a thumbnail was pierced in his right ankle, and a chunk of flesh and bone had been torn from both his sides.
The less fatal penetrating, stabbing, and cutting wounds were countless.
Staggering, he got to his feet.
Jin gripped his sword tightly and surveyed his surroundings.
Is this... the final legacy left by Solderet?
It was dark.
There wasn't a speck of light, and he couldn't see an inch ahead.
When he created a ball of flame on his palm to light up the surroundings, all he could see was his own shadow.
Drip, drip...
He could see the drops of blood from his body seeping into the floor.
Even though the floor was as hard as rock, it left no trace.
He had experienced this type of subspace a few times already.
Jin began to move forward with a limping gait.
Time was of the essence.
The time in the subspace and the outside world probably flowed differently, but he had to get his power and return as quickly as possible.
Power.
The reason Jin had sought this place, the reason so many had sacrificed themselves.
-It's not shadow energy, nor chaotic energy... it seems to be an authority of a higher dimension, Brother Van.
-The youngest wouldn't be talking nonsense... for now, that's good news. If you get that power, you'll become stronger, right?
He recalled the moment he had first found the entrance to the legacy.
That day, from the barrier surrounding the legacy, Jin had first encountered the existence of an authority superior to spiritual energy.
A black energy that couldn't be named.
It felt as if he could become the 'one true god' Kelliac spoke of, if he obtained it.
The darkness that now filled the surroundings was that very energy.
Five days ago, just facing this darkness had filled him with a fear that he would lose his humanity, but now he was just desperate.
He just wanted to obtain the black power as quickly as possible, go outside, and defeat Kelliac.
He just wanted to avenge the people, the world.
"Hah, hah...!"
His body was getting heavier due to the extreme blood loss.
No more true energy was flowing from Temar's left arm.
"Valeria! Solderet...!"
Jin shouted.
The moment he thought he might just collapse while walking through the legacy like this, he saw a faint light in the distance.
A lonely blue light, like a single star in a cloudy night. It was clearly Hister's magic.
"Valeria!"
Can't she hear me? Or did I see it wrong?
Jin's heart grew urgent, and he moved towards the light, shouting repeatedly.
It wasn't an illusion. The light was definitely getting closer with every step he took.
A landmark had appeared in the vast emptiness.
Enduring the pain and dizziness was not a difficult task compared to the outside.
'Just like when I saved Sister Runtia from the evil god's subspace in the past, Valeria is showing me the way...!'
The moment he thought that, Jin realized that the light he had seen was not just a recording window.
It was Valeria.
She was collapsed on the floor, holding a blue light.
"...Valeria!? Valeria, get a grip!"
The Valeria Hister from another world. It was definitely her.

She had helped the Coalition find their way through the Plutonian Cannon's blast when they were fighting the Demon Army's Genesis Knights, and she had saved Jin's life by stopping time the moment Kelliac had begun to awaken the Sun God's power.
If it weren't for her, Jin wouldn't even be here right now.
Jin knew instinctively.
The reason Valeria was collapsed here now was the price for all of that.
It felt like his heart was sinking. Jin hastily checked on Valeria.
Her entire body was covered in wounds deeper and more serious than his own.
"Ugh... ugh... J-Jin..."
Your wounds are deep, so don't say anything for now. I'll go get someone.
Such words almost came out reflexively.
But in this bleak and desolate space, there were only Jin and Valeria.
No one could help them.
Then what should he say?
Should he ask what happened? Should he thank her, apologize first, or should he ask for the way to obtain the legacy's power since her breath was shallow?
He didn't know. But Valeria was different.
"It's really... you. What a relief... I'll just... take some of your magic."
Valeria's cold palm touched Jin's chest.
Jin stroked her head as he felt his magic slowly draining into her palm.
They stayed like that for a long while.
A much more relaxed breathing sound was heard from Valeria, who had finished absorbing the magic.
But she wasn't fundamentally healed.
"Hoo, I think I can talk with this much."
Soon, Valeria raised her upper body and met Jin's eyes.
She stared at Jin without even blinking.
As if to store him in her eyes.
It was a strange feeling.
Jin had entrusted Valeria's corpse to Luet and come here.
But such a familiar face was looking at him.
In some ways, it was a gaze that felt even closer than that of the dead Valeria.
"You must have a lot of questions."
"I'll tell you on the way. This is the entrance of the legacy. To get Solderet's power, you have to go to the end."
Jin nodded and carried her on his back.
She had only recovered a little of her energy by absorbing magic; she was not in a state to walk.
The wounds on Jin and Valeria's bodies were touching.
Some wounds opened wider, and some wounds strangely overlapped just right, and the bleeding stopped.
He could feel the blood from their wounds flowing into each other's bodies.
"You can go in that direction."
Jin began to walk in the direction Valeria's finger was pointing.
He couldn't run fast either, as his wounds were deep.
It also felt like Valeria wouldn't be able to endure it if he went too fast.
"I didn't expect to see you in Solderet's legacy."
"This future was designed by him and me. Rokia helped with the creation of the subspace, but that's all. She and Solderet didn't see eye to eye."
Designed. At that word, Jin's brow furrowed.
"...Valeria, did you know I would come here?"
"To some extent."
"Then did you and Solderet know from the beginning that the world would eventually meet its end at the hands of Kelliac Zipple and the Demon Army?"

"Neither Az Mil's foresight, nor Olta's ability to handle time, nor the witch's and Solderet's power, nor Kinzelo's authority, nor the Origin Stone. The future can never be read accurately, no matter how great the power. Those authorities are just like high mountains."
"High mountains?"

"Yes. If you look at a river from right in front of it, you can't know where it flows until you follow the water's path to the end. But if you look down from a high mountain or the sky, you can grasp its flow at a glance, right? It's like that."
To some extent.
That was why Valeria had answered Jin's question that way.

"But if you look from far away, you can see the flow right away, but you can't know what's happening inside. Who comes to drink water from that river, who is polluting that river. You only find out after the phenomenon has grown large enough to be seen from afar. So, I was always anxious. Whether the future I designed was the right one, whether the person I chose could really change the water's path that was only flowing towards ruin, no matter what they did..."
The person I chose. Jin repeated those words in his mind.
And the next moment, Valeria continued with these words.
"Jin, you were not originally the person Solderet first chose."
